headline: Guidance raised on record leasing despite EPS dip
summary_short: Federal Realty posted Q2 2026 diluted EPS of $0.97, down from $1.78 a year ago mainly on a smaller real-estate gain and the absence of a 2025 tax credit, while Core FFO per share rose 6.8% y/y to $1.88 on record leasing volume and rent spreads.
summary_long: Reported net income fell y/y mainly because Q2 2026 included a $20.6M gain on real-estate sales versus $76.5M a year ago, plus the absence of a one-time $13.0M tax-credit benefit booked in Q2 2025; Core FFO, which excludes that credit, rose 6.8% per share to $1.88 on record leasing (124 comparable leases, 819,273 sq ft, +15% cash / +28% straight-line rent spreads) and portfolio occupancy of 93.8%. Federal Realty raised and tightened full-year 2026 guidance: EPS to $4.22-$4.30 (from $3.94-$4.03) and Nareit/Core FFO per share to $7.48-$7.56 (from $7.46-$7.55). It raised the quarterly dividend 3% to $1.16/share -- a 59th consecutive annual increase -- and ended the quarter with $107.2M cash against $4.77B total debt.

drivers.explanation: CEO Donald Wood framed the quarter around record leasing activity and outsized FFO growth, attributing it to productivity from existing real estate, which underpins the raised long-term FFO/AFFO growth framework introduced at the May 2026 Investor Day.

Rental income rose to $325.9M from $302.5M y/y; the release ties this broadly to an all-time-record 819,273 sq ft of comparable leasing at +15% cash / +28% straight-line rent spreads, though it gives no line-item cause for consolidated revenue specifically.

This KPI is Property Operating Income (POI): $232.1M actual vs $213.2M y/y grew because revenue (+7.8% y/y) outpaced combined rental expense + real-estate tax growth; the release separately discloses like-for-like Comparable Property POI growth of 2.8%, with the remainder from non-comparable (redevelopment/acquisition) properties.

Sequential and y/y declines track a much smaller gain on sale of real estate this quarter ($20.6M) versus an implied ~$92.7M in Q1 2026 (six-month total $113.3M minus Q2's $20.6M) and $76.5M in Q2 2025; the release does not itself compare to Q1.
Mirrors the Operating income move above -- both reflect the same swing in gain on sale of real estate across the three periods.
Tracks the operating-income decline above; a higher depreciation & amortization addback ($100.6M vs $89.2M y/y) partially offsets it but the gain-on-sale swing dominates.

The release states the y/y decline was primarily driven by a lower gain on the sale of real estate this quarter ($20.6M vs $76.5M) and, to a lesser extent, the absence of a one-time tax credit benefit recognized in Q2 2025.
The release explicitly attributes the EPS decline to the year-over-year drop in gain on sale of real estate and the absence of the 2025 new-market tax-credit transaction income.
Mirrors the Diluted EPS move above; same net-income decline against a comparable basic share count (86.18M vs 85.97M y/y).
